A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same Length-MAX Tokenizer paper, with 29 readable pages including appendices A–P. Text and rendered-page comparison establish that all paper content is identical; only the first-page arXiv version/date stamp and its position differ.

before.justification: v1 reports original tokenizer evaluations, GPT-2 training and inference experiments, downstream benchmark results, and system measurements in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original empirical results, including measured GPT-2 results at 124M, 355M, and 1.3B parameters in Table 2 and system benchmarks in Tables 20–21.

M1.justification: The frequency-times-length objective, scoreboard-based greedy procedure, Rabin-Karp enumeration, and longest-prefix/DFA application remain identical in Section 3 and Appendix N.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same FineWeb and RefinedWeb data, domain evaluations, GLUE tasks, seven extended benchmarks, TinyStories evaluation, and character-noise scenario. Appendix coverage is unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in corresponding experiments: BPE, WordPiece, and SentencePiece in the tokenizer and GLUE comparisons; BPE in extended benchmarks; and HuggingFace tokenizers BPE in Tables 20–21.

E3.justification: The reported corpus sizes, model configurations, vocabulary sizes, metrics, training settings, noise level, and system benchmarking procedures are unchanged in Section 4 and Appendices K–M and P.

E4.justification: Both versions retain identical vocabulary-scaling, noise-robustness, vocabulary-utilization, word-boundary, and Zipf analyses, as well as the same qualitative token examples and generated-output case study.

E5.justification: Five-run reporting, the listed random seeds, mean±standard deviation, paired t-tests, confidence intervals, and the 10,000-resample paired bootstrap are identical, including Appendices F, J, K, and P.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and qualitative findings match, including appendix results. For example, Table 4 retains BPE latency of 517±9 ms versus Length-MAX at 446±7 ms, and Table 5 retains macro scores of 0.366 versus 0.413.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 retains identical coverage definitions, graph-partitioning equations, NP-hardness argument, and monotonicity reasoning. Complexity statements and the FLOPs-based scaling derivation are also unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain exactly the same claims about compression, training and inference efficiency, downstream quality, theoretical guarantees, and implementation contributions.

C2.justification: The explanations involving shorter sequences and redistributed token-frequency mass are unchanged. Section 6 retains the same limitations concerning English-only validation, model scale, frozen checkpoints, and vocabulary-size suitability.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, software versions, seeds, and resource-release statements are identical, including Appendices K–P. The arXiv stamp update adds no reproducibility information.

R1.justification: Section 2, the reference list, and all research-positioning statements are identical, including the claimed complementarity with SuperBPE and discussion of token-free alternatives.

P1.justification: Only the first-page arXiv stamp changes from v1, dated 25 November 2025, to v2, dated 8 August 2026. The title, authors, prose, terminology, section order, and appendices are unchanged.

P2.justification: The updated arXiv stamp is repositioned slightly rightward and downward in the first-page margin. All figures, tables, captions, equations, and body layouts are identical; pages 2–29 render identically.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, supporting evidence, explanations, limitations, and reproducibility information are identical throughout both PDFs and their appendices. Updating and repositioning the arXiv stamp produces no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
